name: Layout and Spacing Rulebook
summary: Hierarchy, spacing scale, rhythm, grid and adapting to every screen.
check: Blur a screenshot: the focal point and groups are still clear.

rules.title: Most important first
rules.text: People read top to bottom and from the start edge. The main message and action sit near the top and the leading side (`DC-07`, `PE-02`).

rules.title: The squint test
rules.text: Blur the screen (or squint): you should still see one clear focal point, then two or three groups. If everything has equal weight, nothing leads.

rules.title: Progressive disclosure
rules.text: Show what most people need; put the rest behind a link, a disclosure, a tab or the next page. Do not put every option on the first screen.

rules.title: Separate controls from content
rules.text: Navigation and toolbars look like controls; content looks like content. A floating bar over content needs a clear edge or a scroll-edge fade, not a heavy box.

rules.title: One spacing scale on a 4 px base
rules.text: For example 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Every margin, padding and gap comes from it (`DC-05`).

rules.title: Proximity groups
rules.text: Space inside a group is clearly smaller than space between groups (at least about 1.5–2×). Spacing groups before borders or backgrounds do (`DC-08`, `SL-12`).

rules.title: Vary the rhythm
rules.text: A page with the same gap everywhere is monotonous. Dense passages earn quiet ones; section spacing is larger than block spacing, which is larger than element spacing.

rules.title: Use `gap`
rules.text: Lay out with flex/grid `gap` instead of margins on children, so spacing stays consistent and no stray margin collapses.

rules.title: Comfortable padding
rules.text: Cards and buttons have enough inner padding that text never touches the edge; on phones, body text keeps at least 16 px from the screen edge (never under 12 px).

rules.title: A grid with a reason
rules.text: A 12-column (or 4/8 on mobile) grid with fixed gutters, and content that sometimes breaks it on purpose. Align edges: things that look aligned must be aligned.

rules.title: Alignment and indentation show hierarchy
rules.text: Items on the same edge read as siblings; indented items read as children. Do not centre everything.

rules.title: Every section as a centred stack
rules.text: Mix compositions: split, offset, full-bleed image, list, table, long text. A row of equal cards is the template (`SL-09`, `SL-57`).

rules.title: Real content widths
rules.text: Text blocks capped by measure (`TY-10`); images and data allowed wider; the page container about 1200–1440 px with fluid side padding.

rules.title: Same function on every size
rules.text: A smaller screen may show less at once (sidebar becomes a drawer, a table becomes cards or scrolls) but never removes a feature.

rules.title: Container queries for components
rules.text: Components adapt to the space they get (`@container`), not only to the viewport, so the same card works in a sidebar and a main column.

rules.title: Respect safe areas
rules.text: `env(safe-area-inset-*)` for fixed bars on phones with notches and home indicators; sticky CTAs sit above the home indicator (`PE-03`).

rules.title: Reserve space for media
rules.text: Images, videos, embeds and ads have `width`/`height` or `aspect-ratio`, so nothing jumps while loading (`PF-03`).

rules.title: A compact sticky header
rules.text: A sticky header stays short (about 56–72 px on desktop, less on phones) and may hide on scroll down and return on scroll up.

rules.title: Horizontal scroll on the page
rules.text: Nothing overflows the viewport sideways at any width from 320 px up. Wide tables and carousels scroll inside their own container.

rules.title: Fixed heights on text containers
rules.text: Boxes that hold text grow with it. Fixed heights cut off translations, larger text and user zoom.

rules.title: Full-width lines on large screens
rules.text: On wide screens text never runs edge to edge; the measure stays capped (`TY-10`) even when the layout is wide.

rules.title: Content hidden behind sticky elements
rules.text: Sticky headers, footers, cookie bars and chat buttons never cover focused elements, anchors or the last line of content (`AX-17`).

rules.title: Every page works on a phone
rules.text: Build and check every page at 320, 360, 390 and 430 px, not only desktop: nothing overflows sideways, text fits its box and is start-aligned (`TY-25`), images are cropped or swapped for the narrow frame where needed, controls are at least 44 px, the navigation stays reachable, and every feature still works (`LY-14`, `LY-19`, `AX-08`).

rules.title: Air between sections on phones
rules.text: Phones get their own spacing, not the desktop values scaled down: about 64–96 px between sections, 32–48 px between blocks inside a section and at least 12–16 px between related elements, with 16–24 px side padding (`LY-09`). If a phone screen looks crowded, add space before shrinking text.

rules.title: Full-height sections in dvh
rules.text: A section meant to fill the screen uses `min-height: 100dvh` (or `100svh` when it must not jump as the browser bar hides), never `100vh`, which on phones is taller than the visible screen and hides the bottom under the browser bar (`LY-16`).
